# Venusflytrap — Benchmark Results

*Generated by `venusflytrap bench`. Deterministic corpus: seed=1337, 2000 samples each of benign / attack / obfuscated (6000 total).*

These numbers are **measured locally on an open, synthetic corpus**. They are not a claim about production traffic. The false-positive count is reported in full — Venusflytrap does not assert "zero false positives" (see docs/RESEARCH.md §C7).

## Detection quality

| Engine | Recall (all) | Recall (obfuscated) | Precision | F1 | FP | FP rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Regex baseline | 29.4% | 17.8% | 100.0% | 0.454 | 0 | 0.000% |
| Tokenizer baseline | 100.0% | 100.0% | 85.2% | 0.920 | 694 | 34.700% |
| Venusflytrap (full) | 96.2% | 96.1% | 100.0% | 0.981 | 0 | 0.000% |

## Reading the result

- The regex baseline should collapse on the obfuscated set (encoding/case/comment mutations) — this is claim C1 in RESEARCH.md, reproduced.
- The tokenizer baseline recovers much of the recall but at a higher false-positive rate, because it flags lone dangerous tokens without checking that they form a reachable construct.
- The full engine should keep obfuscated recall high **and** FP low, because the graph/taint step distinguishes a formed attack from a coincidental keyword.
